subject.title: [Feature]: openclaw models status --probe --all — per-model health check across all configured models

question: Should OpenClaw add `models status --probe --all` as a first-class core CLI mode for all configured models, or fold that behavior into broader fallback-chain or staged model-migration work?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the new flag would make real provider requests across configured primary, fallback, image, and possibly agent-specific models, so maintainers need to own the token/rate-limit, output, JSON, and overlap contract before automation implements it.

options.title: Approve Scoped Status Probe
options.body: Add opt-in `models status --probe --all` with conservative timeout/concurrency, provider/profile filtering, JSON output, docs, focused tests, and redacted live proof.

options.title: Fold Into Model Safety Workflow
options.body: Make fallback-chain testing or staged model migration own configured-model verification, and keep this issue as product context for that broader UX.

options.title: Defer Core CLI Probe
options.body: Keep current auth probes and point users to external dashboards or manual checks until maintainers want a core all-model live probe contract.

recommendation.title: Approve Scoped Status Probe
recommendation.body: Add opt-in `models status --probe --all` with conservative timeout/concurrency, provider/profile filtering, JSON output, docs, focused tests, and redacted live proof.

likelyOwner.reason: He introduced the current auth-probe surface and has the strongest history plus prior product-scoping review on this cluster.
